metadata.title: Local limit theorems and counting for transverse subgroups
metadata.abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. We study the joint distribution of partial Cartan projections and the two associated Cartan flags for Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups. Assuming local mixing of the associated Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure, we prove two local limit theorems and deduce counting asymptotics in Euclidean balls and tubes, together with equidistribution of the Cartan flags. These qualitative conclusions hold for $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, for which the local mixing hypothesis is satisfied. If the group is linearly $\theta$-regular near the direction of maximal growth, a polynomial error in local mixing gives polynomial errors in these results. Applying the quantitative local mixing theorem of Kim-Oh-Pan, we obtain local limit and counting theorems with polynomial error estimates for several classes of relatively Anosov representations of Fuchsian groups.
